original_question: Fix d - 2 < s < d and consider the annulus B_{r,R} = {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}. Find the equilibrium measure mu* supported on B_{r,R} that minimizes the Riesz s-energy I_s(mu) = integral integral K_s(x - y) dmu(x) dmu(y) among all probability measures supported on that annulus.
target_in_paper: Edward Saff's open problem "Equilibrium measure on an annulus" (the multi-dimensional annulus equilibrium problem).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it uses the same parameter range d-2 < s < d, the same geometric set (an annulus in R^d), and the same variational characterization of the equilibrium measure as a probability measure minimizing the Riesz s-energy over measures supported on that annulus.
missing_details: State explicitly that 0 < r < R, so B_{r,R} is the closed annulus {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}.
Specify the admissible class as Borel probability measures mu on R^d with supp(mu) contained in B_{r,R}.
Define the Riesz s-kernel explicitly; the paper introduces the kernel just before stating the annulus problem, while your draft leaves K_s implicit.
Clarify that the question is to determine the annulus equilibrium measure in the same sense as the preceding ball problem recalled in the paper.
Keep the scope exactly to the regime d-2 < s < d; the paper does not broaden this annulus problem in that section to other s-ranges or other external-field variants.
Because the paper is an open-problems collection, the faithful wording should present this as an open determination/characterization problem, not as a solved explicit formula.
refined_question:
Let d >= 2 and let s satisfy d-2 < s < d. For fixed radii 0 < r < R, define the closed annulus B_{r,R} := {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}. Determine the Riesz s-equilibrium measure of B_{r,R}; that is, determine a Borel probability measure mu on R^d with supp(mu) subseteq B_{r,R} such that mu minimizes the Riesz s-energy
I_s(mu) := ∬ |x-y|^{-s} dmu(x) dmu(y)
among all Borel probability measures supported on B_{r,R}.
justification: The draft is targeting the Edward Saff section, not any Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3, because arXiv:2312.07754 is a workshop open-problems collection rather than a single theorem-driven paper. The abstract says the paper collects open problems, the introduction says each section lists an open problem, and Saff's section is explicitly titled "Equilibrium measure on an annulus." In that section, the paper first recalls the Riesz-energy setup and the classical ball problem of Riesz, then states the annulus version as the open problem. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply the annular analogue of the ball equilibrium problem, with the missing stand-alone details being the annulus parameters, the admissible class of measures, and the explicit kernel definition.
